answer: Each new identity must lock a ferrous stake in a tundra escrow that cannot thaw for several epochs, and publish a one-time cipher of a secret known only to that identity. Peers attest only when the cipher is unused and the escrow is intact. If two names open the same preimage, or if the stake is pulled early, the peer set slashes the ferrous bond in full. Spinning up N sybils therefore costs N isolated stakes plus the tundra wait, which peers enforce by withholding attestations and burning colliding escrows.
